sentences.show: Papillon. The most famous prison escape ever written. A man who floated off Devil's Island on a sack of coconuts.
But French records say he was never on Devil's Island at all.
Henri Charrière, a Paris crook nicknamed Papillon, the butterfly. In 1931 he got life for murder, and swore he was innocent.
He was shipped to the penal colony of French Guiana.
In his book, he escapes again and again, survives solitary, and ends up on Devil's Island, the prison nobody leaves.
He studies the waves, then jumps into the sea on a sack of coconuts, and rides the tide away.
He reaches Venezuela, goes free, and opens restaurants in Caracas.
The book sold 1.5 million copies in France, and became a Hollywood movie.
But the prison files say he worked in the colony hospital, where escaped convicts told him their stories.
And those famous cliffs on Devil's Island? The island slopes gently into the sea.
Even his heroic rescue of a girl from sharks, critics say another convict did it, and lost both legs.
A French ministry said divide his story by ten to get near the truth. Charrière said it was 75 percent true.
In 2005, a man of 104 said he was the real Papillon. With a butterfly tattoo too.
Butterflies fly away. Don't. Stay, and subscribe.
